a2a.governance-linux-foundation.claim: The A2A Protocol is an open source project under the Linux Foundation, contributed by Google.

a2a.governance-tsc.claim: A2A is maintained by a Technical Steering Committee with representatives from eight named organizations.

a2a.latest-version.claim: The newest entry in the A2A changelog is 1.0.1, dated 2026-05-26.

aaif.a2a-growth-stage.claim: A2A's post says the protocol was accepted as a Growth Stage project at the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF).

aaif.founding.claim: MCP's announcement says it will become a founding project of the newly created Agentic AI Foundation, a directed fund under the Linux Foundation co-founded by Anthropic, Block and OpenAI.

aaif.projects-a2a-post.claim: A2A's post refers to MCP, goose and AGENTS.md as sibling projects of AAIF.

agentsmd.definition.claim: AGENTS.md is described by its own README as a simple, open format for guiding coding agents.

agentsmd.stewardship.claim: The agents.md website states that AGENTS.md is stewarded by the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation.

anthropic.bea-agents.claim: Anthropic defines agents as systems where LLMs dynamically direct their own processes and tool usage.

anthropic.bea-published.claim: Anthropic's 'Building effective agents' was published on 2024-12-19.

anthropic.bea-start-simple.claim: Anthropic advises finding the simplest solution possible and increasing complexity only when needed.

anthropic.bea-tooling-changed.claim: Anthropic's own 2024 post carries a note that much of its tooling landscape has changed since December 2024.

anthropic.bea-workflows.claim: Anthropic defines workflows as systems where LLMs and tools are orchestrated through predefined code paths.

anthropic.ctx-attention-budget.claim: Anthropic describes LLMs as having an attention budget that they draw on when parsing large volumes of context.

anthropic.ctx-context-rot.claim: Anthropic describes context rot: recall accuracy decreases as the number of tokens in the context window increases.

anthropic.ctx-definition.claim: Anthropic defines context engineering as curating and maintaining the optimal set of tokens during LLM inference.

anthropic.ctx-published.claim: Anthropic's 'Effective context engineering for AI agents' was published on 2025-09-29.

anthropic.harn-initializer-agent.claim: Anthropic's initializer agent runs the first session with a specialized prompt that sets up the environment, including init.sh, a progress log file and an initial git commit.

anthropic.harn-progress-file.claim: Anthropic says the claude-progress.txt file, alongside git history, lets a fresh agent quickly understand the state of work.

anthropic.harn-published.claim: Anthropic's 'Effective harnesses for long-running agents' was published on 2025-11-26.

anthropic.harness-changes-move-results.claim: Anthropic reports that, after fixing bugs and using a less constrained scaffold, Opus 4.5's score jumped to 95%.

anthropic.harness-counterpoint.claim: Anthropic says each harness component encodes an assumption about what the model can't do on its own, and those assumptions can quickly go stale as models improve.

anthropic.multi-agent-tokens.claim: Anthropic reports that, in its data, agents typically use about 4× more tokens than chat interactions and multi-agent systems about 15× more tokens than chats.

anthropic.multi-agent-when.claim: Anthropic says multi-agent systems excel at valuable tasks with heavy parallelization, information that exceeds single context windows, and interfacing with numerous complex tools, and that domains where all agents must share the same context or have many dependencies between agents are not a good fit today.

anthropic.postmortem-2025-causes.claim: Anthropic's postmortem names three bugs, by these headings: a context window routing error, output corruption, and an approximate top-k XLA:TPU miscompilation.

anthropic.postmortem-2025-issues.claim: Anthropic's postmortem describes three bugs that caused the degradation, and gives when each occurred and how it was resolved.

anthropic.twt-meaningful-context.claim: Anthropic's second tool-writing principle is returning meaningful context from tools back to agents.

anthropic.twt-namespacing.claim: Anthropic's first tool-writing principle is namespacing tools to define clear boundaries in functionality.

anthropic.twt-published.claim: Anthropic's 'Writing effective tools for agents' was published on 2025-09-11.

anthropic.twt-token-efficiency.claim: Anthropic's third tool-writing principle is optimizing tool responses for token efficiency.

api.cache-control-top-level.claim: A top-level cache_control field on the request turns on automatic caching, which puts the cache breakpoint on the last cacheable block.

api.cache-invalidation-effort.claim: Changing output_config.effort always invalidates message blocks.

api.cache-invalidation-hierarchy.claim: Cache order is tools, then system, then messages, and a change at one level invalidates that level and every level after it.

api.cache-invalidation-images.claim: Adding or removing images anywhere in the prompt affects only the messages cache.

api.cache-invalidation-system-web-search.claim: Enabling or disabling web search modifies the system prompt, and the table marks the system and messages caches as invalidated (the tools cache is not).

api.cache-invalidation-thinking.claim: Changing the thinking configuration always invalidates message blocks, and tool and system caches on models that render it ahead of them.

api.cache-invalidation-tool-choice.claim: Changing tool_choice invalidates only the messages cache; the tools and system caches remain valid.

api.cache-invalidation-tool-definitions.claim: Modifying tool definitions (names, descriptions, parameters) invalidates the entire cache.

api.cache-output-unchanged.claim: The docs say prompt caching has no effect on output token generation, and the response is identical to the one you would get without caching.

api.cache-prefix-whole-match.claim: A cache hit requires 100% identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control.

api.cache-read-refreshes-ttl.claim: The docs say the default cache lifetime is 5 minutes and that the cache is refreshed at no extra cost each time cached content is used.

api.cache-ttl-default-5m-and-1h.claim: The default cache TTL is 5 minutes, and a 1-hour TTL is available at 2x the base input token price.

api.cache-usage-fields.claim: The docs list cache_creation_input_tokens and cache_read_input_tokens as cache fields in a response's usage, and input_tokens counts only the tokens after the last cache breakpoint.

api.compaction-each-kind-own-header.claim: Each compaction kind has its own beta header, so each page has its own list.

api.compaction-on-demand-beta-header.claim: On-demand compaction is in beta and uses the compact-2026-09-04 beta header.

api.compaction-on-demand-parameter.claim: On-demand compaction is requested with a top-level compaction parameter of type summarize.

api.compaction-threshold-beta-header.claim: Threshold compaction is in beta and uses the compact-2026-01-12 beta header.

api.compaction-threshold-strategy.claim: Threshold compaction is enabled by adding a compact_20260112 strategy to context_management.edits.

api.consecutive-turns-combined.claim: The Messages API combines consecutive user or assistant turns in a request into a single turn.

api.console-api-keys.claim: API keys for the Claude API live in the Claude Console, where one is created on the Settings → API keys page.

api.content-multiple-blocks.claim: A response's content is an array of content blocks, each with a type that determines its shape.

api.context-editing-beta-header.claim: Context editing is in beta and is enabled with the context-management-2025-06-27 beta header.

api.context-editing-clear-thinking.claim: The clear_thinking_20251015 strategy manages thinking blocks from earlier assistant turns.

api.context-editing-clear-tool-uses.claim: The clear_tool_uses_20250919 strategy clears tool results when context grows beyond a configured threshold.

api.effort-default-medium-opus-5-5-haiku.claim: Most Claude models default to high effort; Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 default to medium.

api.effort-five-levels.claim: The effort page says Claude Fable 5.1 supports all five effort levels.

api.effort-location.claim: Effort is set with output_config.effort on the request.

api.effort-max-availability.claim: The effort page lists the models on which the max level is available.

api.effort-not-all-max-support-xhigh.claim: Not every model that supports max also supports xhigh.

api.effort-xhigh-availability.claim: The effort page lists the models on which the xhigh level is available.

api.error-400-invalid-request.claim: HTTP 400 carries error type invalid_request_error for a request format or content problem.

api.error-401-authentication.claim: HTTP 401 carries error type authentication_error, meaning there is an issue with the API key.

api.error-429-rate-limit.claim: HTTP 429 carries error type rate_limit_error when a rate limit, spend cap or Claude Code workspace limit is reached.

api.error-429-retry-after.claim: A rate-limit 429 response includes a retry-after header that says how long to wait.

api.error-429-spend-cap-no-retry-after.claim: A tier spend-cap 429 has no retry-after header and keeps failing until access resumes.

api.error-500-api-error.claim: HTTP 500 carries error type api_error for an unexpected internal error.

api.error-504-timeout.claim: HTTP 504 carries error type timeout_error when the request timed out while processing.

api.error-529-overloaded.claim: HTTP 529 carries error type overloaded_error, meaning the API is temporarily overloaded.

api.error-sdk-retries.claim: The official SDK retries transient failures twice by default with exponential backoff, honoring retry-after when present.

api.max-tokens-incomplete-tool-use.claim: If a max_tokens response is cut off inside a tool use block, the docs say to retry with a higher max_tokens value to get the full tool use.

api.messages-create-endpoint.claim: Creating a message is a POST to /v1/messages.

api.messages-stateless.claim: The Messages API is stateless: you send the full conversational history with each request.

api.models-entry-id.claim: Each entry in the Models API list has an id, which is a unique model identifier.

api.models-list.claim: The Models API response (GET /v1/models) shows which models are available for use in the API; more recently released models are listed first.

api.parallel-results-one-message.claim: For parallel tool use, the docs mark one user message per tool result as Wrong and all tool results together in a single user message as Correct.

api.prefill-claude-4-6-and-later.claim: Claude 4.6 and later models and Claude Mythos Preview do not support assistant prefill; a prefilled last assistant message returns HTTP 400 invalid_request_error.

api.prefill-claude-fable-5-1.claim: Claude Fable 5.1 returns a 400 error when the assistant message is prefilled.

api.prefill-claude-haiku-5-5.claim: Claude Haiku 5.5 rejects a prefilled final assistant turn with a 400 error, even with thinking turned off.

api.prefill-claude-opus-5-5.claim: Claude Opus 5.5 rejects a messages array that ends with a prefilled assistant turn.

api.prefill-claude-sonnet-5-5.claim: Claude Sonnet 5.5 rejects a prefilled last assistant turn with a 400 error, as Claude Sonnet 4.6 and Claude Sonnet 5 do.

api.prefill-thinking-on-or-off.claim: Claude 4.6 and later models reject a prefilled final assistant turn with a 400 error whether or not thinking is on.

api.retry-after-meaning.claim: retry-after is the number of seconds to wait before retrying, and earlier retries fail.

api.sdk-env-api-key.claim: In the Python SDK, passing api_key is optional: its default reads the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY environment variable.

api.sdk-max-retries-option.claim: The Python SDK's Anthropic client takes a max_retries option, whose default is DEFAULT_MAX_RETRIES.

api.split-results-teach-serial.claim: The parallel tool use docs say that formatting tool results incorrectly in the conversation history 'teaches' Claude to avoid parallel calls.

api.stop-reason-end-turn.claim: end_turn is the stop reason when Claude finished its response naturally.

api.stop-reason-field.claim: Every Messages API response includes a stop_reason field that tells why Claude stopped generating.

api.stop-reason-max-tokens.claim: max_tokens is the stop reason when the response reached the request's max_tokens limit.

api.stop-reason-model-context-window-exc.claim: model_context_window_exceeded is the stop reason when the response stopped because it reached the model's context window limit.

api.stop-reason-pause-turn.claim: pause_turn is the stop reason when a server-tool loop reached its iteration limit.

api.stop-reason-refusal.claim: refusal is the stop reason when Claude declined to generate a response, returned as a normal HTTP 200 response rather than an error.

api.stop-reason-stop-sequence.claim: stop_sequence is the stop reason when Claude emitted one of the request's stop_sequences.

api.stop-reason-tool-use.claim: tool_use is the stop reason when Claude is calling a tool and expects the application to run it.

api.streaming-event-types.claim: A streamed response is a sequence of events: message_start, then for each content block content_block_start, content_block_delta events and content_block_stop, then message_delta and message_stop.

api.structured-outputs-citations-incompa.claim: Enabling citations together with output_config.format returns a 400 error.

api.structured-outputs-ga.claim: Structured outputs is generally available on the Claude API.

api.structured-outputs-json-param.claim: JSON outputs are requested with output_config.format of type json_schema.

api.structured-outputs-output-format-dep.claim: The output_format parameter has moved to output_config.format and is deprecated.

api.structured-outputs-parse-helper-arg.claim: The Python parse helper takes the Pydantic model as an output_format argument, and the SDK sends it as output_config.format.

api.structured-outputs-prefill-incompati.claim: Message prefilling is incompatible with JSON outputs.

api.structured-outputs-strict-tool-use.claim: Strict tool use is set with strict: true and guarantees schema validation of tool names and inputs.

api.system-prompt-role.claim: The docs say a system prompt is a way of providing context and instructions to Claude, such as specifying a particular goal or role.

api.temperature-deprecated-after-opus-4-.claim: On models released after Claude Opus 4.6, temperature is deprecated: 1.0 is accepted for backwards compatibility and any other value is rejected with a 400 error.

api.temperature-range.claim: The temperature parameter defaults to 1.0 and ranges from 0.0 to 1.0.

api.thinking-adaptive-recommended.claim: Anthropic says to use adaptive thinking wherever both thinking modes are available.

api.thinking-billed-as-output.claim: The docs say the tokens Claude uses while thinking are billed as output tokens.

api.thinking-blocks-pass-back-tool-use.claim: During tool use, thinking blocks from the assistant turn must be passed back complete and unmodified alongside the tool_use block.

api.thinking-blocks-preserve.claim: Within the latest assistant message, the consecutive thinking blocks must match what the model generated: they cannot be rearranged, edited or partially dropped.

api.thinking-budget-tokens-deprecated.claim: Manual thinking with type enabled and budget_tokens is deprecated on Claude 4.6 models, where requests still succeed, and is rejected with HTTP 400 on Claude 4.7 and later.

api.thinking-display-default-omitted.claim: The docs name omitted as the default display setting on the listed models, including Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5.

api.token-count-endpoint.claim: Token counting is a POST to /v1/messages/count_tokens.

api.token-count-response.claim: The token-count response contains the total number of input tokens.

api.token-count-status.claim: Token counting is generally available on the Claude API.

api.tool-choice-adaptive-forced-exceptio.claim: Forced tool use works with adaptive thinking, except that Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 reject it on every request with a 400 error.

api.tool-choice-manual-thinking-allowed.claim: With manual extended thinking (thinking type enabled), tool_choice may only be auto or none; any and tool return an error.

api.tool-choice-unsupported-fallback.claim: Where forced tool use is not supported, tool_choice any and tool fail while auto and none still work.

api.tool-result-blocks-first.claim: In the user message that carries tool results, every tool_result block comes before any text content in that message.

api.tool-result-ids-must-match.claim: A tool_result's tool_use_id is the id of the tool use request that the result answers.

api.tool-result-is-error.claim: is_error is an optional tool_result field that is set to true when the tool execution resulted in an error.

api.tool-result-text-after-results.claim: Any text in the tool-result user message must come after all tool results.

api.tool-result-unrun-call.claim: A tool_use block that is not run still needs a tool_result with is_error true and a brief explanation.

api.tool-results-are-data.claim: The docs say Claude treats tool-result content as untrusted data, so instructions placed in tool results may be ignored or flagged as a potential injection.

api.tool-results-single-user-message.claim: The docs say to return one tool_result for each tool_use block, all together in the next user message.

api.tool-use-without-result-error.claim: Leaving out the tool_result for a tool_use makes the request fail with the standard error 'tool_use ids were found without tool_result blocks immediately after'.

api.usage-input-output-tokens.claim: The Messages API reference's usage object has input_tokens and output_tokens, the numbers of input and output tokens used.

evals.grader.claim: Anthropic defines a grader as logic that scores some aspect of the agent's performance; a task can have several graders.

evals.outcome.claim: Anthropic defines the outcome as the final state in the environment at the end of the trial.

evals.pass-at-k.claim: pass@k measures the likelihood that an agent gets at least one correct solution in k attempts (Anthropic's definition).

evals.pass-hat-k.claim: pass^k measures the probability that all k trials succeed (Anthropic's definition).

evals.published.claim: Anthropic's 'Demystifying evals for AI agents' was published on 2026-01-09.

evals.task.claim: Anthropic defines a task as a single test with defined inputs and success criteria.

evals.tau-successor.claim: Anthropic's evals page calls 𝜏-Bench and its successor τ2-Bench benchmarks that incorporate multidimensionality.

evals.transcript.claim: Anthropic defines a transcript (also called trace or trajectory) as the complete record of a trial.

evals.trial.claim: Anthropic defines each attempt at a task as a trial.

harnesses.cc-auto-mode.claim: The docs name the permission mode auto, which lets everything run without asking, with background safety checks.

harnesses.cc-compaction.claim: Claude Code compacts automatically as the context window approaches its limit, and its automatic pass works the same way as the /compact step.

harnesses.cc-hooks.claim: Claude Code's hook events PreToolUse and PostToolUse fire on every tool call inside the agentic loop, except EndConversation calls, which skip both.

harnesses.cc-mcp.claim: Claude Code can connect to external tools and data sources through the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

harnesses.cc-memory-files.claim: Claude Code's CLAUDE.md locations include ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md for the user and ./CLAUDE.md or ./.claude/CLAUDE.md for the project.

harnesses.cc-permission-modes.claim: The docs name Claude Code's permission modes default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk and bypassPermissions, and give what each runs without asking.

harnesses.cc-plan-mode.claim: The docs say plan mode tells Claude to research and propose changes without making them: Claude reads files and runs shell commands to explore, writes a plan, and does not edit the source; edits stay blocked until the plan is approved, except in interactive terminal sessions with bypass permissions available.

harnesses.cc-sandbox.claim: Claude Code's Bash sandbox uses the operating system's own isolation: the built-in Seatbelt framework on macOS, and bubblewrap and socat on Linux and WSL2.

harnesses.cc-subagents.claim: Each subagent runs in its own context window, with a custom system prompt, specific tool access and independent permissions.

harnesses.codex-agents-md.claim: Codex collects every AGENTS.md from the project root down to the current working directory and concatenates them.

harnesses.codex-approval-modes.claim: Codex's approval policy values are untrusted, on-request and never: untrusted requires approval for commands unless an exec policy rule allows them, on-request lets the model decide when to ask the user, and never does not ask the user to approve commands.

harnesses.codex-sandbox-modes.claim: Codex's sandbox modes, by the repository's serde names, are read-only (the default), workspace-write and danger-full-access.

harnesses.mini-swe-agent-mit.claim: mini-swe-agent is released under the MIT License.

jsonschema.additional-properties-false.claim: Setting additionalProperties to false means no additional properties will be allowed.

jsonschema.enum.claim: enum: an instance validates successfully if its value is equal to one of the elements of the enum array.

jsonschema.required.claim: required: an object instance is valid against it if every item in its array is the name of a property in the instance.

jsonschema.type.claim: type restricts an instance to the primitive types null, boolean, object, array, number and string, and to integer, which matches a number with a zero fractional part.

mcp.annotation-destructive.claim: destructiveHint: if true, the tool may perform destructive updates to its environment.

mcp.annotation-idempotent.claim: idempotentHint: if true, calling the tool repeatedly with the same arguments has no additional effect on its environment.

mcp.annotation-openworld.claim: openWorldHint: if true, the tool may interact with an open world of external entities.

mcp.annotation-readonly.claim: readOnlyHint: if true, the tool does not modify its environment.

mcp.annotations-hints.claim: The spec schema states that all ToolAnnotations properties are hints that may not faithfully describe tool behaviour.

mcp.annotations-names.claim: The ToolAnnotations interface in the spec schema declares a readOnlyHint boolean member.

mcp.annotations-untrusted-schema.claim: The spec schema says clients should never make tool-use decisions based on ToolAnnotations received from untrusted servers.

mcp.annotations-untrusted-tools.claim: The 2026-07-28 tools page requires clients to treat tool annotations as untrusted unless they come from trusted servers.

mcp.auth-basis.claim: The 2026-07-28 authorization page lists the OAuth 2.1 IETF draft (draft-ietf-oauth-v2-1-13) among the specifications its mechanism is based on.

mcp.auth-oauth21-must.claim: Implementors of the 2026-07-28 spec MUST follow OAuth 2.1 security best practices.

mcp.auth-optional.claim: Authorization is OPTIONAL for MCP implementations in the 2026-07-28 spec.

mcp.client-features-2025-11-25.claim: The 2025-11-25 index lists Sampling, Roots and Elicitation as features clients may offer to servers.

mcp.client-features-2026.claim: The 2026-07-28 index lists Elicitation as the feature clients may offer to servers; Sampling and Roots are not in that list.

mcp.deprecated-guidance.claim: The 2026-07-28 changelog says new implementations should not adopt deprecated features.

mcp.deprecated-roots-sampling-logging.claim: The 2026-07-28 revision deprecates the Roots, Sampling and Logging features.

mcp.docs-latest-label.claim: The MCP docs navigation labels revision 2026-07-28 as the latest spec version.

mcp.ga-announcement.claim: MCP's GA post announces the 2026-07-28 specification release.

mcp.governance-aaif.claim: Anthropic is donating MCP to the Agentic AI Foundation, a directed fund under the Linux Foundation.

mcp.governance-lf-neutral.claim: MCP's announcement says the Linux Foundation will not dictate the technical direction of MCP.

mcp.latest-revision.claim: The MCP spec repo sets LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION to 2026-07-28.

mcp.release-tag.claim: The commit tagged 2026-07-28 has the subject 'Merge pull request #3158 from modelcontextprotocol/claude/subscriptions-listen-envelope'.

mcp.server-discover.claim: The 2026-07-28 revision adds a server/discover RPC that servers MUST implement.

mcp.server-features.claim: The 2026-07-28 index lists Resources, Prompts and Tools as features servers offer to clients.

mcp.sessions-removed.claim: The 2026-07-28 revision removes protocol-level sessions and the Mcp-Session-Id header from Streamable HTTP.

mcp.stateless-core.claim: The 2026-07-28 revision removes the initialize/notifications/initialized handshake to make MCP stateless.

mcp.tasks-extension.claim: The 2026-07-28 revision moves experimental tasks out of the core protocol into an official extension named io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks.

mcp.transport-http-sse-changelog.claim: The 2026-07-28 changelog reclassifies the HTTP+SSE transport (deprecated since protocol version 2025-03-26) as Deprecated under the feature lifecycle policy.

mcp.transports-standard.claim: The transports page describes stdio as newline-delimited messages over the standard streams of a client-launched subprocess.

mcp.transports-streamable-http.claim: The transports page says each Streamable HTTP message is an HTTP POST to a single MCP endpoint.

models.aliases.claim: Dateless model IDs are their own pinned snapshots, and the alias row repeats them.

models.cache-min-1024-tokens.claim: The minimum cacheable prompt is 1,024 tokens for Opus 4.8, Sonnet 5 and Sonnet 4.6.

models.cache-min-2048-tokens.claim: The minimum cacheable prompt is 2,048 tokens for Opus 4.7.

models.cache-min-4096-tokens.claim: The minimum cacheable prompt is 4,096 tokens for Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.5.

models.cache-min-512-tokens.claim: The minimum cacheable prompt is 512 tokens for Fable 5.1, Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, Opus 5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5, Mythos 5 and Haiku 5.5.

models.cache-read-multiplier.claim: Cache reads cost 0.1x base input, 0.025x on Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1, and 0.05x on Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5.

models.cache-write-1h-multiplier.claim: A 1-hour cache write costs 2x base input price and is valid for 1 hour.

models.cache-write-5m-multiplier.claim: A 5-minute cache write costs 1.25x base input price and is valid for 5 minutes.

models.context-window.claim: The models overview lists a 1M-token context window for each of the four current models.

models.fable-5-1-price.claim: Claude Fable 5.1 base input is $10 per MTok, output $50 per MTok, and cache hits $0.25 per MTok.

models.haiku-5-5-price-over-100k.claim: Claude Haiku 5.5 for prompts over 100,000 tokens is $0.50 input, $2.50 output and $0.05 cache hit per MTok.

models.haiku-5-5-price-up-to-100k.claim: Claude Haiku 5.5 for prompts up to 100,000 tokens is $0.10 input, $0.50 output and $0.01 cache hit per MTok.

models.ids-current.claim: The models overview gives Claude API IDs claude-fable-5-1, claude-opus-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 and claude-haiku-5-5 for the four current models.

models.max-output.claim: The models overview lists 128K max output tokens for each of the four current models.

models.opus-5-5-price.claim: Claude Opus 5.5 base input is $4 per MTok, output $20 per MTok, and cache hits $0.20 per MTok.

models.sonnet-5-5-price.claim: Claude Sonnet 5.5 base input is $2 per MTok, output $10 per MTok, and cache hits $0.10 per MTok.

otel.attr-request-model.claim: gen_ai.request.model holds the name of the model a request is made to.

otel.attr-system-deprecated.claim: The core CHANGELOG (v1.38.0) refers to gen_ai.system as a deprecated attribute.

otel.attr-system-renamed.claim: gen_ai.system was renamed to gen_ai.provider.name in semantic conventions v1.37.0 (breaking change).

otel.attr-tool-call-id.claim: gen_ai.tool.call.id is the tool call identifier.

otel.attr-tool-name.claim: gen_ai.tool.name is the name of the tool used by the agent.

otel.attr-usage-input.claim: gen_ai.usage.input_tokens counts the tokens used in the GenAI input (prompt).

otel.attr-usage-output.claim: gen_ai.usage.output_tokens counts the tokens used in the GenAI response (completion).

otel.genai-moved-repo.claim: Core semantic conventions deprecated their gen_ai.* definitions and moved them to a dedicated GenAI repository.

otel.genai-registry-version.claim: The GenAI registry manifest declares schema_url gen-ai-dev/1.42.0-dev.

otel.genai-stability.claim: The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions registry manifest declares stability: development.

otel.op-chat.claim: The chat member of gen_ai.operation.name is described as a chat completion operation.

otel.op-execute-tool.claim: For tool execution spans, gen_ai.operation.name SHOULD be execute_tool.

otel.op-invoke-agent.claim: For the invoke_agent client span, gen_ai.operation.name SHOULD be invoke_agent.

otel.span-chat-name.claim: The inference client span name SHOULD be '{gen_ai.operation.name} {gen_ai.request.model}'.

otel.span-create-agent-name.claim: The create_agent client span name SHOULD be 'create_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}'.

otel.span-execute-tool-name.claim: The execute_tool span name SHOULD be 'execute_tool {gen_ai.tool.name}'.

otel.span-invoke-agent-name.claim: The invoke_agent span name SHOULD be 'invoke_agent {gen_ai.agent.name}' when gen_ai.agent.name is readily available.

owasp.asi-asi01-agent-goal-hijack.claim: ASI01 in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications is titled 'Agent Goal Hijack'.

owasp.asi-asi02-tool-misuse-exploitation.claim: ASI02 in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications is titled 'Tool Misuse & Exploitation'.

owasp.asi-asi05-unexpected-code-executio.claim: ASI05 in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications is titled 'Unexpected Code Execution (RCE)'.

owasp.asi-asi06-memory-context-poisoning.claim: ASI06 in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications is titled 'Memory & Context Poisoning'.

owasp.asi-asi07-insecure-inter-agent-com.claim: ASI07 in the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications is titled 'Insecure Inter-Agent Communication'.

owasp.asi-list-version.claim: The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (ASI) mapping file is labelled version 2026 and announced 2025-12-09.

owasp.llm-2026-release.claim: The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026 has a release date of August 4, 2026.

owasp.llm01-2025-definition.claim: In the 2025 edition LLM01:2025 Prompt Injection was defined as user prompts altering LLM behaviour or output in unintended ways.

owasp.llm01-2026-definition.claim: LLM01:2026 Prompt Injection defines a prompt-injection vulnerability as input that alters model behaviour in ways the developer did not intend, including via retrieved content, tool output and persistent memory.

owasp.llm03-2026-agentic-mapping.claim: The 2026 LLM03 entry maps Excessive Agency in agentic systems to ASI02, ASI03 and ASI08.

owasp.llm03-2026-definition.claim: LLM03:2026 Excessive Agency defines the vulnerability as damaging actions performed in response to unexpected, ambiguous or manipulated LLM outputs, whatever the cause.

owasp.llm03-2026-excessive-agency.claim: The 2026 edition's Excessive Agency heading is LLM03:2026.

owasp.llm06-2025-excessive-agency.claim: The 2025 edition's LLM06 heading is Excessive Agency.

owasp.llm06-2026-definition.claim: LLM06:2026 Unbounded Consumption covers excessive, uncontrolled inference that enables service disruption, financial cost or model cloning.

owasp.llm06-2026-unbounded-consumption.claim: The 2026 edition's LLM06 heading is Unbounded Consumption.

papers.react-authors.claim: The ReAct BibTeX in the authors' repo lists Shunyu Yao, Jeffrey Zhao, Dian Yu, Nan Du, Izhak Shafran, Karthik Narasimhan and Yuan Cao as authors.

papers.react-title-id.claim: The ReAct authors' repo cites ReAct as arXiv 2210.03629, titled 'ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models', ICLR 2023.

papers.tau-bench-eprint.claim: The tau-bench authors' BibTeX gives eprint 2406.12045 with archivePrefix arXiv.

papers.tau-bench-title-id.claim: The tau-bench authors' BibTeX gives the title 'τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains' and year 2024.

papers.tau-passk-code.claim: tau-bench's code adds comb(c, k) / comb(num_trials, k) for each task, where c counts that task's successful trials.

skills.maintainer.claim: The Agent Skills format was originally developed by Anthropic and released as an open standard.

skills.progressive-disclosure.claim: The Agent Skills spec describes progressive disclosure: agents load skills progressively, adding detail only as a task requires it.

skills.progressive-tier1.claim: Under progressive disclosure, the name and description of every skill are loaded at startup (about 100 tokens).

skills.required-description.claim: The description field is required, with a maximum of 1024 characters, and describes what the skill does and when to use it.

skills.required-name.claim: The name field is required, at most 64 characters, and limited to lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens.

skills.spec-frontmatter.claim: The Agent Skills specification requires SKILL.md to contain YAML frontmatter followed by Markdown content.
